newsitem.title: USA: Nike says orders rise 66 pct, top record.
newsitem.headline: Nike says orders rise 66 pct, top record.

text.p: Nike Inc, the athletic footwear maker, said Monday its global future orders through the holiday season are up 66 percent over the year ago period to a record $3.5 billion.
In a statement along with its first quarter earnings, the company attributed the sharp increase to growth in its core shoe business and a change in its shipping procedures.

The company also approved a two-for-one split of the company's Class A and Class B common shares, payable as a 100 percent dividend on October 23 to shareholders of record at the close of business on October 11.

In its first quarter, ended August 31, Nike earned net income of $226.1 million, or 1.53 a share, on revenues of $2.28 billion versus net income of $182.1 million, $1.25 a share, on sales of $1.7 billion last year.

"Brand strength, which many thought was nearing its peak last year, continues to grow unabated in fiscal 1997," said Philip Knight, chief executive, "propelling Nike to the best quarter in our history, record futures orders, and another stock split for our shareholders.
For the first quarter, Nike's gross margins slipped slightly from last year to 40.3 percent from 40.4 percent.
Selling, general and administrative expenses rose to 23.2 percent of revenues versus 21.7 percent last year.
In the U.S., men's basketballs shoes showed a 48 percent increase in sales from the year ago first quarter while sales of men's running shoes were up 50 percent.
Women's fitness shoes in the U.S. posted a 45 percent increase in sales in the first quarter, and women's sports shoes jumped 68 percent.
U.S. apparel sales grew 93 percent from the year ago.
Overseas, revenues rose 35 percent from last year with Britain, Italy and Germany the leading nations. In the Asia Pacific, all countries posted sales gains over 35 percent.
Nike shares were up 2-3/4 at 123 in mid-morning trade.
